BillHeading.Sponsors: Representatives Young, Shea, Taylor, Buys, and Hargrove

BillHistory.ReferredCommittee: Referred to Committee on Early Learning & Human Services.

BillHeading.BriefDescription: Providing that home-based instruction of a foster child may not be the sole basis for denying a foster-family home license.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to homeschooling foster youth; adding a new section to chapter 74.15 RCW; and creating a new section.

BillSectionHeader.P: In August 2016, the department of social and health services proposed changes to foster parent licensing forbidding the provision of home-based instruction to all children in the care and custody of the department. This rule was made effective September 19, 2016, as WAC 388-148-1525.

BillSection.P: As home-based instruction can be an appropriate and effective educational model for foster youth, the legislature intends to reverse WAC 388-148-1525(1)(b) and allow foster parents to provide home-based instruction to foster youth.

BillSection.BillSectionHeader: Sec. 2. A new section is added to chapter 74.15 RCW to read as follows:
BillSection.P: The department shall not deny a foster-family home license on the sole basis that a foster youth in his or her care received home-based instruction as described in RCW 28A.225.010(4).
